page: Microsoft Azure L96as_v4 is a high-capacity server instance belonging to the Lasv4 family, powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture, it features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz and includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 8.0 GB of RAM per core.

A defining feature of the L96as_v4 is its massive local storage capacity, consisting of 23,038 GB of NVMe SSD storage. This local storage is Premium Storage capable, designed for high-throughput and low-latency data access. The instance runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier performance in multi-core processing and memory bandwidth. The server achieved top 10% rankings in stress-ng multi-core CPU tests, Geekbench multi-core scores, and PassMark CPU encryption. Memory bandwidth for small-block cached reads reached 7,287.47 GB/sec, while large-block uncached reads and writes performed in the top 25% at 229.38 GB/sec and 140.83 GB/sec, respectively. It also demonstrated strong database capabilities, processing 122.77 million Redis SET operations per second and scoring in the top 25% for PassMark database operations.

Given the substantial local NVMe storage density combined with 768 GB of RAM and 96 vCPUs, the L96as_v4 offers high qualitative cost efficiency for resource-intensive deployments that would otherwise require multiple smaller nodes. It is highly suited for large-scale relational and non-relational databases, data warehousing, high-throughput web serving, software compilation pipelines, and memory-intensive analytics workloads.
